mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which is likely to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business activity increase.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 100,000 but SPX 20-day returns are negative in over 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% indicates tighter monetary policy, which is expected to lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs increase and corporate earnings are pressured.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases below 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates a tight labor market with rising inflation, which is likely to lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed may raise rates more aggressively.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% year-over-year signals strong demand in the housing market, which is likely to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries (e.g., construction, furniture) experience growth.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 10% YoY but SPX 60-day returns are negative in over 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals increased economic activity, which is likely to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenues and earnings improve.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real consumer spending (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening demand, which is likely to lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer-driven industries experience slowing sales.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decreases by more than 1% MoM but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals weakening economic activity, which is likely to lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth slow.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows by more than 0.5% QoQ but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is rising by more than 0.2% month-over-month, it indicates a potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic uncertainty increases.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE increases by > 0.2% month-over-month
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.
